text: Requests seem to take a very long time, even for things that I would expect to be fast, like loading this page or opening the create PR modal. 1. Let's figure out why it's actually slow and try to fix it. 2. Every link/button in the design system should have a loading state (based on the `ko-loading` attribute, probably?). If nothing else, in some cases we can rely on deferred loading in Koda, but that should be rarely needed.

The project page and the Push modal are slow mostly for one reason. Every request reads the full state of every branch by starting git processes one after another, and runs a lot of git commands that it doesn't need. Those git calls are synchronous (`execFileSync`), so while one of them runs the whole server waits. A request that should be fast gets stuck behind a slow one. I've only read the code, not timed it, so the order below comes from counting git calls, not from measurements.

## 1. Why it's slow

**The biggest cost is one `git show` per file.** On the project page, each branch's stories are built from `storiesOf` → `groupsOf` → `incrementOf` (`server/main.js:328`, `server/main.js:842`, `server/increment.js:83`). `incrementOf` lists the design's files at the branch's starting point, then reads each one with its own git process (`server/increment.js:86`, `server/increment.js:106`). That's every view, every state and every approved snapshot. A design here has 30–60 snapshot files (`prelude/design-workspace/snapshots/`, `prelude/build/snapshots/`), and starting a process on Windows costs tens of milliseconds. So one branch can take seconds.

On top of that, for each branch:
- `branches.status` runs about 8 git commands, starting with `mainBranch`, and runs twice per branch: once from `branchState` (`server/main.js:717`) and once from `groupsOf` (`server/main.js:859`).
- `designCommitsSince` runs once per group, plus `merging` and `remoteOf`.
- `branchState` parses every session transcript on the branch (`server/main.js:709`), so it gets slower as history grows.

**Where this happens:**
- **Loading the project page** (`GET /f/<id>`, `server/main.js:493`) works out everything for every branch.
- **The work region** (`/f/<id>/work`) does it again. It reloads on every `needs-changed` and `projects-changed` event (`server/views/projects/page.eta:58`), which means every time any turn starts or ends, plus every 5 minutes. While an agent is working, this keeps blocking the server.
- **The Push modal** (`GET …/branches/<b>/publish`) calls `branchNow()` (`server/main.js:383`). That runs `branchesOf` for every branch, stories and all, just to find one. `_publish.eta` doesn't use the stories at all. When the modal is loaded directly rather than as a fragment, it also builds the whole page.

**Fetching from the remote blocks too.** The page and the work region call `tidy()` → `tidyFolder` (`server/main.js:810`). At most every 30 seconds per project, this runs a synchronous `git fetch origin` (`server/branches.js:527`), a network call made while everything else waits.

## 2. Loading states

Koda already does most of this. It sets `ko-busy` on the link or button whose request is out, and `ko-loading` / `aria-busy` on the region being loaded (Koda's reference, lines 3074, 3308–3341, 2154). The design system barely uses it. The only rule is `button[ko-busy], form[ko-loading] .btn { opacity: 0.7; }` (`prelude/prelude-design-system/system/components.css:154`, and the same in `server/public/ds/v1/components.css:115`).

That leaves out:
- every link styled as a button (`a.btn`), including "Push and open a pull request…" (`server/views/projects/_branch.eta:89`);
- `.icon-btn`, `.link-btn` and plain links;
- and even where it applies, a change to 0.7 opacity is hard to notice.

Once the server is fixed, `ko-busy` should be enough almost everywhere. `ko-defer` should rarely be needed.

## What I'd change

**Speed** (in `server/increment.js`, `server/branches.js`, `server/main.js`, `server/project.js`):
- In `incrementOf`, read all the files at the starting point in one `git cat-file --batch`, or compare the blob IDs `filesAt` already returns and only read files that actually changed. Snapshots in particular only need their blob IDs compared.
- Cache each branch's `status` and `groupsOf` results by the branch's latest commit and main's latest commit. Then a refresh where nothing moved costs a couple of `rev-parse` calls, and `groupsOf` uses the `status` already worked out instead of running it again.
- Give `branchesOf` an `only` option, so the Push modal looks up just its one branch, and add `stories: false`, since the modal doesn't use them.
- Run the fetch in `tidyFolder` asynchronously (`spawn`, not `execFileSync`), and send `projects-changed` if tidying removed anything.
- To confirm the order, add a temporary counter and timer to the `git` helper in `branches.js` (behind an environment variable) before changing anything.

**Loading states** (in `prelude/prelude-design-system`):
- In `system/components.css`, replace line 154 with one `[ko-busy]` rule covering `.btn`, `.icon-btn`, `.link-btn` and `a`. It would set the progress cursor, add a small spinner after about 150 ms (so fast requests don't flicker), and add a still version for reduced motion. Then copy it into ds/v1 while pages are still on it.
- Show the busy state in `system/components/button.html`, `icon-button.html` and `screens/02-components.html`. Add a line to `system/guidelines.md` and `RULES.md`: every control shows it's working through `ko-busy`, with nothing written per page, and `ko-defer` only for regions that really are slow.
Fixing this on prelude/fix-requests-seem-to-take-a-very-long-time-even-for-th, made from main. The agent can change the project there now; each turn is committed to the branch.
Let's implement your changes
I'll start with the speed fixes, then the loading states. First, the tests and the parts I haven't read yet.

## 1. Speed

The fixes cut the git calls behind the project page, its work region and the Push modal. Git runs synchronously (each call holds up every request, not just its own), so fewer calls means less waiting everywhere.

- **One git process for all of a branch's original files.** Before, the stories read each file as it was on main with its own `git show`, often 30 to 60 per design. The new `textsOf` (`server/branches.js`) reads them all with one `git cat-file --batch`, and `incrementOf` (`server/increment.js`) uses it.
- **Results are kept until the branch moves.** File contents, file lists and commit lists are stored by their git ids, so they can't go stale. `branches.status` now checks with one `git for-each-ref` call whether the branch, main or the remote's main has moved, and reuses its last answer if none has. Before, it ran about 8 git commands, twice per branch. Now it runs once, and `groupsOf` uses its answer.
- **The Push modal reads only its own branch, without stories.** `branchesOf` has a new `only` option for this.
- **The `git fetch` no longer blocks requests.** It now runs in the background (`fetchRemote`), and tidying happens after it finishes. A merge done locally is still tidied at once, so the page answers with the branch already gone.

One behaviour change: a pull request merged on GitHub now leaves "In progress" a moment after the project page loads, when its regions reload, instead of as it loads. The views and states are unchanged, and I noted this in `prelude/project-landing-page/NOTES.md`.

## 2. Loading states

Koda already sets `ko-busy` on whatever was pressed until its request is answered, so no page needed changing. The new rules in the design system's `components.css` (copied into ds/v1):
- **Buttons** (`.btn`, `.link-btn`): a small spinner beside the words, after 150 ms so quick answers don't flicker.
- **Icon buttons and plain links:** the glyph or the words pulse.
- **All of them:** the cursor changes to the progress cursor.
- **Reduced motion:** a still spinner ring and no pulse. The cursor still changes.

The delay and spin speed are two new tokens, `--delay-busy` and `--duration-spin`. I added guideline 12 to the design system's guidelines: every control shows it's working through `ko-busy`, and `ko-defer` is only for regions that are slow on their own. No page needed `ko-defer`. The busy state is also shown in `button.html`, `icon-button.html` and the gallery screens.

## Tests

Run `npm test`. The ones most affected:
- `test/branches.test.js` has a new test that the original files are read in one go, and that a branch's status updates once it moves.
- `test/build.test.js`: the remote test now waits for the tidy that follows the page load.
- `test/increment.test.js`, `test/app.test.js` and `test/fixes.test.js` cover code I changed.

## Left as it was

`branchState` still reads every session transcript on a branch each time. That's file reading, not git, but it grows with history. If a long-running branch is still slow, that's the next thing to look at.

The fix's notes, with what to check, are in `prelude/fixes/requests-seem-to-take-a-very-long-time-even-for-things/NOTES.md`.
